package_info.why_malicious: The package contains advanced command-and-control (C2) malware that exfiltrates host data and establishes a reverse shell using covert network techniques, including CDN abuse and HTTP-based C2, to evade detection and provide attackers with remote access.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code crafts an HTTPS request to pypi.python.org with a manipulated Host header, causing Fastly CDN to forward the request to the attacker's C2 server, exfiltrating encoded payload data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code abuses CDN infrastructure to covertly exfiltrate data to an attacker-controlled domain, making detection by network monitoring tools difficult.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not manipulate Host headers to redirect traffic through CDN infrastructure to attacker-controlled servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: CDN Host header manipulation may be used in advanced multi-tenant SaaS architectures, but never for exfiltrating user data.
key_indicators: Manipulation of Host header in HTTPS requests
Use of PyPI domain as a cover for C2 communication

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after receiving a C2 command, the code executes arbitrary shell commands from the attacker, captures the output, encodes it, and sends it back to the C2 server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing attacker-supplied shell commands and exfiltrating their output is a hallmark of remote access trojans and backdoors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never execute arbitrary remote commands or exfiltrate command output.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may execute commands, but only with explicit user consent and authentication.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of command output to remote server

attack_chain.action: Malware sends an HTTPS request to pypi.python.org with a manipulated Host header, exfiltrating initial payload (e.g., hostname) to the attacker's C2 server via Fastly CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: C2 server receives victim information and can initiate further interaction.

attack_chain.action: C2 server responds with a command payload; malware decodes and executes the command on the victim machine.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of arbitrary attacker-supplied commands on the victim.

attack_chain.action: Malware captures the output of the executed command, encodes it, and sends it back to the C2 server via HTTP POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives command output and can continue interactive control (reverse shell).

behavioral_signatures: Outbound HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with non-standard Host headers
Base64-encoded data in query strings to /images or similar paths
Execution of shell commands based on remote HTTP responses
file_indicators: Presence of code manipulating Host headers in Python requests
References to psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net or similar Fastly subdomains
network_indicators: HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with Host header set to psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net
Subsequent HTTP traffic to Fastly CDN endpoints not matching normal PyPI usage
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python processes making HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with suspicious Host headers (e.g., psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net). Flag base64-encoded data in query strings to /images endpoints. Detect subprocess or shell command execution triggered by remote HTTP responses. Correlate with unusual outbound traffic patterns to CDN infrastructure.
